headline: No budget moves this week: LinkedIn stays paused, Meta is above target in every model, and the direct surge is fading (71 to 43 conversions) while AI-sourced answers stay elevated.

tests.hypothesis: Google's last-touch credit (68.6%) overstates its incremental value; first-touch gives 39.3% (ROAS 5.9 vs 10.2). Part of its conversions may be demand created by AI assistants, email or Meta.
tests.design: Geo holdout: pause or cut by 50% in about 20% of matched regions for 3 to 4 weeks, with brand and non-brand split. Measure total conversions (including direct) in test vs control regions. Keep the other channels unchanged. Success means a conversion drop in test regions that matches the credit Google claims.

flag_verdicts.reason: Meta CPA is $60 to $97 since 10-02, but spend is already trimmed (weekly $3.5k to $2.5k). Last 3 weeks CPA is up 18%, under the 40% trigger. Last week CPA improved to $83.57 and ROAS is 2.16. Implied ROAS is 2.66-4.16 across models, above the 1.5 target. No cut.

Already paused since 11-02 and spend is $0. Tracked conversions were 0 for the two weeks before the pause, on $2.4-2.6k a week. Self-reported LinkedIn has been 0% for 4 weeks. Keep paused. The tracking audit and relaunch test from last run is still pending.
The 09-12 to 09-18 spike is over. CPA held at $20.56 vs $18.33, and the last 3 weeks' CPA is $17.61 vs $17.57 earlier.

Direct rose from 38 to 71 a week, then fell to 43 in the latest week. Paid spend is flat or down. Self-reported AI answers (assistant plus ChatGPT) are 17-28% in recent weeks vs about 4% in August, so this is consistent with AI-driven demand. No paid channel is credited and no budget is moved. The latest dip needs another week to read.

flags.message: meta CPA rose 1.6x, from $60 to $97, starting 2026-10-02.
linkedin CPA rose 19.1x, from $148 to $2825, starting 2026-10-17.
google_search spend jumped for 7 days (2026-09-12 to 2026-09-18); CPA held at $21 vs $18. Likely fine, confirm before acting.
Direct conversions grew 5.9x (1.5 to 8.9/day) while paid spend moved 0.85x. Self-reported AI answers went from 6% to 26%. Something untracked is driving buyers.
